title: Module 1 Knowledge Check
description: Eight questions on the foundations and models of instructional design. Unlimited attempts; best score counts.

questions.text: Which statement best captures the systems view of instruction?
options: Instruction is a sequence of lectures followed by a test
Instruction is a set of interacting components whose interactions determine the outcome, so changing one component affects the others
Instruction is whatever the subject-matter expert decides to present
Instruction is a product that can be built without analysis if the designer is experienced
questions.feedback: The systems view is why analysis precedes design and evaluation closes the loop.

questions.text: A manager asks you to build a course because sales are down. Which instructional design step should come first?
options: Conduct a needs assessment to determine whether a performance gap exists and whether instruction can close it
questions.feedback: Many performance problems are not training problems. Needs assessment decides whether instruction is the right solution.

questions.text: In the Dick and Carey model, which order guarantees alignment?
questions.feedback: Objectives first, assessments second, strategies third. The same logic underlies Backward Design.

questions.text: Which model cycles through prototype, review, and revision with stakeholders reviewing working versions early and often?
questions.feedback: SAM is the agile alternative to a linear ADDIE.

questions.text: Which of the following are among Merrill's First Principles of Instruction? Select all that apply.
options: Learners engage in solving real-world problems
New knowledge is applied by the learner
New knowledge is integrated into the learner's world
questions.feedback: Problem-centered, activation, demonstration, application, integration. Delivery mode is not a principle.

questions.text: Backward Design asks the designer to plan learning activities before deciding what evidence of learning will be acceptable.
questions.feedback: Backward Design plans desired results first, acceptable evidence second, and learning experiences third.

questions.text: The Kemp model is drawn as a circle rather than a line to signal that:
options: The designer can begin with any element and the elements are interdependent
It is only for online courses
questions.feedback: The circular layout expresses flexibility and interdependence, with ongoing processes surrounding the elements.

questions.text: Which pairing of problem type and model is most defensible?
options: High-stakes safety procedure with clear performance outcomes: Dick and Carey
High-stakes safety procedure with clear performance outcomes: unguided rapid prototyping with no formative evaluation
Ill-defined problem with available stakeholders: a strict waterfall ADDIE with sign-off before any building
Curriculum unit planning: no model at all
questions.feedback: High-stakes, well-defined performance favors the rigor and formative evaluation of Dick and Carey.
